\chapter{Two modern-technology words, retrieved twice}
\label{ch:sa-modern-technology-retrieval}
\hlchaptermodality{270}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can retrieve the familiar words for computer and internet from meaning.}

Complete chapter 270 by independently retrieving internet and computer in a second order.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[(independent modern-technology …]{Two modern-technology words: round one}

\label{lesson:SA-C270-modern-technology-first-retrieval}



\begin{quote}
Prepare to retrieve two familiar nouns from their English meanings.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn: independent retrieval}
No Sanskrit model is shown before you answer.

Say the Sanskrit for these meanings, in order: a computer, then the internet.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built: check after answering}]
Now check: \textbf{\sk{संगणकम्}} (\emph{saṅgaṇakam}) is “a computer,” and \textbf{\sk{अन्तर्जालम्}} (\emph{antarjālam}) is “the internet.”
\end{grammarlens}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
You have completed one two-word retrieval. It shows recall of two nouns, not a claim about using either technology.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(independent modern-technology …]{Two modern-technology words: round two}

\label{lesson:SA-C270-modern-technology-final-retrieval}



\begin{quote}
Prepare to retrieve the same two meanings in a fresh order.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn: independent retrieval in a fresh order}
No Sanskrit model is shown before you answer.

Say the Sanskrit for these meanings in the reverse order: the internet, then a computer.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built: check after answering}]
Now check: \textbf{\sk{अन्तर्जालम्}} (\emph{antarjālam}) is “the internet,” and \textbf{\sk{संगणकम्}} (\emph{saṅgaṇakam}) is “a computer.”
\end{grammarlens}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
You can retrieve two modern-technology nouns twice without a visible model. This is not evidence of device use, internet navigation, digital literacy, technological competence, human validation, learner attainment, or exam readiness.
\end{tcolorbox}
